name: British Museum
description: One of the world's great museums, with the Rosetta Stone, Egyptian mummies and the Parthenon sculptures. Permanent collection is free.
tip: Pick two or three galleries rather than trying to see everything.
checkNote: Some galleries open later on certain days and special exhibitions are ticketed.

name: National Gallery
description: Western European paintings from the 13th to the early 20th century, including Van Gogh's Sunflowers and Turner. Free to enter.
tip: Free guided talks and Friday late openings run at set times; check the site.
checkNote: Special exhibitions are ticketed.

name: National Portrait Gallery
description: Portraits of the people who shaped British history, from Tudor monarchs to modern icons. Free to enter; reopened after major refurbishment in 2023.
tip: Start at the top floor for the Tudor galleries and work down.
checkNote: Opening hours vary by day and it opens late some evenings.

name: Tate Modern
description: Modern and contemporary art in the old Bankside power station. The collection displays and the Turbine Hall installations are free.
tip: The Turbine Hall is free and often hosts large commissions.
checkNote: Paid exhibitions are separate. Some days it opens later.

name: Tate Modern viewing level
description: Free viewing terrace on level 10 of the Blavatnik Building with 360-degree views of St Paul's, the City and the Thames.
tip: Go before sunset for the best light. Hours follow the museum.
checkNote: The viewing level can close in bad weather or at busy times.

name: Tate Britain
description: British art from 1500 to today, including Turner, Constable, the Pre-Raphaelites and Hockney. The collection is free.
tip: The Turner galleries are a quiet corner on busy days.
checkNote: Special exhibitions are ticketed.

name: Victoria and Albert Museum
description: The world's largest museum of art, design and performance, from fashion to ceramics and the Cast Courts. Free to enter.
tip: The John Madejski Garden courtyard is a calm place to sit.
checkNote: Friday late opening can vary, and exhibitions are ticketed.

name: Young V&A
description: A museum for children and young people, with play, design and toy collections. Entry is free.
tip: Check the site for a timed free slot to avoid queues at weekends.
checkNote: Booking a free timed slot may be advised at busy times.

name: V&A East Storehouse
description: A free open-access store at Stratford where thousands of objects are on view and you can order an object to see up close. Opened in 2025.
tip: Ordering an object to view usually needs booking ahead.
checkNote: Opening days vary; check before travelling.

name: Science Museum
description: Hands-on galleries on space, medicine, energy and technology. Entry to the main galleries is free.
tip: The Wonderlab and some exhibitions are paid; the main galleries need no ticket.
checkNote: Some exhibitions and the Wonderlab are ticketed. Free entry may need a booked slot at busy times.

name: Natural History Museum
description: Dinosaurs, the blue whale skeleton in Hintze Hall, minerals and the Earth galleries. Permanent galleries are free.
tip: Go early on weekends and school holidays to beat the queue.
checkNote: Special exhibitions are ticketed.

name: Imperial War Museum London
description: How war has shaped lives, from the First World War to today, including the Holocaust and Second World War galleries. Free to enter.
tip: The Holocaust Galleries are not suitable for children under 14.
checkNote: Some exhibitions are ticketed.

name: National Maritime Museum
description: Britain's seafaring story, with Nelson's uniform, ship models and the Great Map. Free entry.
tip: Combine it with Greenwich Park next door.
checkNote: Special exhibitions are ticketed.

name: Queen's House
description: Inigo Jones's 17th-century villa, with its Tulip Stairs and royal art collection. Free to enter.
tip: Look up in the Great Hall; the floor pattern and ceiling are the highlight.
checkNote: Some rooms can close for events.

name: London Museum Docklands
description: The history of the Thames, the port and the people of London, in a Georgian warehouse. Main galleries are free.
tip: Check the site for family sessions during school holidays.
checkNote: Some exhibitions are ticketed. Check opening days.

name: Wellcome Collection
description: Free museum and library about health, medicine and what it means to be human. Quirky objects and changing exhibitions.
tip: The reading room has comfy seating and free Wi-Fi.
checkNote: Usually closed on Mondays. Check hours.

name: Sir John Soane's Museum
description: The architect's home, packed with antiquities, paintings and architectural models. Free to enter, with timed entry at busy times.
tip: Queues can be long; booking a free slot or going on a weekday helps.
checkNote: Closed Monday and Tuesday. Candlelit evenings are ticketed.

name: Wallace Collection
description: Old masters, armour and French 18th-century art in a grand townhouse. Free to enter.
tip: The covered courtyard cafe is a pleasant place for a warm-up.
checkNote: Check hours; the house can close for events.

name: Horniman Museum and Gardens
description: Natural history, world cultures and musical instruments, plus 16 acres of gardens with views over London. Museum and gardens are free.
tip: The aquarium and butterfly house are paid; the museum and gardens are free.
checkNote: Aquarium, butterfly house and some exhibitions cost extra. Gardens may have different hours.

name: William Morris Gallery
description: Textiles, wallpaper and design by William Morris in his Georgian family home, set in Lloyd Park. Free to enter.
tip: Lloyd Park next door has a moat and picnic space.
checkNote: Closed Monday and Tuesday. Check hours.

name: Museum of the Home
description: Rooms from different centuries show how Londoners have lived at home, in historic almshouses with a walled garden. Free to enter.
tip: Walk through period rooms from 1600 to today in order.
checkNote: Closed Mondays. Some events are ticketed.

name: Grant Museum of Zoology
description: UCL's collection of animal skeletons and specimens, including the dodo and the quagga. Free to enter.
tip: Small and quick: a good 30-minute stop near the British Museum.
checkNote: Opening days and hours are limited; check before you go.

name: Petrie Museum of Egyptian Archaeology
description: UCL's collection of about 80,000 Egyptian and Sudanese objects, from early pottery to papyri. Free to enter.
tip: Quiet and compact, with a lot packed into a few rooms.
checkNote: Limited opening days and hours; check before you go.

name: Hunterian Museum
description: Anatomical and surgical collections at the Royal College of Surgeons, reopened in 2023. Free to enter.
tip: Some displays show human remains and may not suit everyone.
checkNote: Check opening days before you go.

name: Bank of England Museum
description: The story of the Bank, from 1694 to today, with a gold bar you can lift and Roman and modern banknotes. Free to enter.
tip: Closed at weekends, so pair it with a weekday City walk.
checkNote: Closed weekends and bank holidays. Check hours.

name: Guildhall Art Gallery and Roman Amphitheatre
description: City of London art collection, plus the remains of Roman London's amphitheatre in the basement. Free to enter.
tip: The amphitheatre is the highlight; head downstairs first.
checkNote: Hours vary; check before you go.

name: British Library Treasures
description: Free Sir John Ritblat Treasures gallery, with the Magna Carta, Shakespeare's First Folio and Beatles lyrics. Free public spaces and cafes.
tip: Free to enter the building, with comfy seating and Wi-Fi in public areas.
checkNote: Hours vary by day; check the site. Exhibitions are ticketed.

name: Serpentine Galleries
description: Contemporary art in two galleries in Kensington Gardens. Free to enter.
tip: Combine with a Kensington Gardens walk and the Serpentine Pavilion in summer.
checkNote: Exhibition changeovers close galleries; check before you go.

name: Whitechapel Gallery
description: Contemporary art gallery in the East End, with changing exhibitions. Free to enter.
tip: Thursday late opening is a good option after work.
checkNote: Closed Mondays. Some exhibitions may be ticketed.

name: Design Museum (free collection display)
description: The free Designer Maker User display explores everyday objects and the thinking behind them. Temporary exhibitions are ticketed.
tip: Only the ground-floor and top collection display is free.
checkNote: Temporary exhibitions cost extra.

name: RAF Museum London
description: Aircraft from early flying machines to jets in historic hangars at Hendon. Free to enter.
tip: The site is large; wear comfortable shoes.
checkNote: Some experiences and parking are paid.

name: National Army Museum
description: The story of the British Army across five centuries, with interactive galleries for families. Free to enter.
tip: Look for family trails and activities in school holidays.
checkNote: Special exhibitions may be ticketed.

name: Brunei Gallery, SOAS
description: SOAS gallery of art and culture from Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Free to enter, with a roof garden.
tip: The roof garden is a hidden spot in Bloomsbury.
checkNote: Closed between exhibitions; check before you go.

name: Sky Garden
description: Free public garden and viewing terrace on top of 20 Fenchurch Street, with views over the Thames. Free tickets must be booked online.
tip: Release dates and times are limited; book as soon as slots open.
checkNote: Booking required; no walk-ins at busy times. Bring photo ID.

name: Horizon 22
description: Free viewing platform on top of 22 Bishopsgate, with views over the City. Booking is required.
tip: Book a sunset slot as early as possible.
checkNote: Booking required; check availability and opening days.

name: The Garden at 120
description: Rooftop garden on the 15th floor of 120 Fenchurch Street. Free to enter.
tip: Quieter than the nearby Sky Garden.
checkNote: Weekday opening only; check before you go and whether booking is needed.

name: One New Change roof terrace
description: Free open-air terrace on top of the shopping centre next to St Paul's Cathedral, with direct views of the dome.
tip: Take the lifts to the top; the terrace is outdoors, so skip in rain.
checkNote: Terrace can close in bad weather; check hours.

name: Parliament Hill
description: A grassy hilltop on Hampstead Heath with a wide view across the London skyline. Free and open at all hours.
tip: A great spot for kite-flying and sunsets.
checkNote: The hill is steep. Paths can be muddy.

name: Primrose Hill
description: A grassy hill north of Regent's Park with one of the best free views of London's skyline.
tip: Pop to the village for coffee, then walk up for sunset.
checkNote: Park hours vary through the year.

name: Greenwich Park
description: Royal park with the Royal Observatory hill, the Prime Meridian line and views to Canary Wharf. The park is free to enter.
tip: Climb the hill for the best view; the Observatory itself charges.
checkNote: Park gates close at dusk; the Royal Observatory is a paid ticket.

name: Kyoto Garden, Holland Park
description: A Japanese garden with a waterfall, koi carp and peacocks inside Holland Park. Free to enter.
tip: Peaceful in the morning; weekends can be busy.
checkNote: Closes at dusk.

name: Crystal Palace Park dinosaurs
description: Victorian life-size dinosaur sculptures from 1854 on islands in a lake, in Crystal Palace Park. Free to visit.
tip: Pair with the maze and the park's cafe and playground.
checkNote: Park gates close in the evening; check seasonal times.

name: Richmond Park
description: Royal park of 2,500 acres with herds of wild red and fallow deer and views of St Paul's. Free to enter.
tip: Keep well back from the deer, especially in autumn.
checkNote: Pedestrian gate times vary through the year.

name: Postman's Park
description: Quiet City garden with the Memorial to Heroic Self-Sacrifice: ceramic plaques for ordinary people who died saving others.
tip: Good place for a quiet lunch break.
checkNote: Open daytime; check seasonal closing times.

name: St Dunstan in the East
description: Bombed-out church ruins turned into a secret garden, with ivy-covered walls. Free to enter.
tip: Often quiet at lunchtime; photographers love it.
checkNote: Opens daytime hours only.

name: Hyde Park
description: One of London's largest royal parks, with a lake (the Serpentine), Speakers' Corner and Kensington Gardens next door. Free.
tip: Walk the Serpentine, then cross into Kensington Gardens.
checkNote: Park hours vary during some events.

name: St James's Park
description: Central royal park with a lake, pelicans, flower beds and views to Buckingham Palace and Horse Guards. Free.
tip: Spot the pelicans near Duck Island.
checkNote: Park hours vary during some events.

name: Regent's Park
description: Royal park with Queen Mary's Gardens, a boating lake, playgrounds and open lawns. Free to enter (the zoo charges).
tip: Queen Mary's Gardens are at their best in June.
checkNote: Closing time changes with the season.

name: Little Venice and Regent's Canal
description: Where the Grand Union and Regent's Canal meet, with painted narrowboats. A towpath walk runs on to Camden. Free.
tip: Walk the towpath from Little Venice to Camden in about 50 minutes.
checkNote: Towpath can be narrow and slippery; check closures.

name: Thames Barrier Park
description: Riverside park with a dramatic green dock, fountains and views of the Thames Barrier. Free to enter.
tip: The fountain jets are a hit with kids on warm days.
checkNote: Closes at dusk; check seasonal times.

name: Leadenhall Market
description: A Victorian covered market with a painted roof, shops and cafes. Free to walk through.
tip: Visit at lunchtime on a weekday when the market is lively.
checkNote: Busiest on weekdays; hours vary by shop.

name: Borough Market
description: Famous food market at the foot of the Shard. Free to enter, with plenty of samples.
tip: Go early on Saturday to avoid crowds; samples are free.
checkNote: Limited trading on other days; hours change at bank holidays.

name: Columbia Road Flower Market
description: Sunday flower market on a pretty East End street, with independent shops and cafes. Free to browse.
tip: Prices fall in the afternoon as stalls sell off flowers.
checkNote: Sundays only. Hours may change at bank holidays.

name: Camden Market
description: Street food, crafts and vintage stalls beside Regent's Canal. Free to browse.
tip: Weekdays are calmer than weekends.
checkNote: Stall hours vary; check before you go.

name: Southbank Centre foyers and free events
description: Free foyer music, exhibitions, the Poetry Library and open-air events on the South Bank, alongside a daily programme of ticketed shows.
tip: Check the free events listing before you go.
checkNote: Free events change daily. Check the what's on page.

name: Barbican Conservatory
description: A tropical conservatory with over 1,500 plant species in the Barbican Centre. Free entry on limited days; booking is required.
tip: Open only on selected days. Book a free ticket as early as you can.
checkNote: Limited opening days; free tickets must be booked; check availability.

name: Choral Evensong at Westminster Abbey
description: Daily sung evening service by the Abbey choir. Attending the service is free; sightseeing visits cost.
tip: Arrive early and keep phones silent: it is worship.
checkNote: Service times vary by day, and some services are closed to the public.

name: Choral Evensong at St Paul's Cathedral
description: Choral Evensong in the cathedral, free to attend. Sightseeing entry is ticketed.
tip: Arrive early; keep phones off and sit where staff guide you.
checkNote: Service times vary by day; check before you go.

name: St Martin-in-the-Fields lunchtime concerts
description: Regular lunchtime concerts in the church beside Trafalgar Square. Free entry, with donations welcome.
tip: Come about 20 minutes early for a good seat.
checkNote: Concert days and times change; check the site.

name: Houses of Parliament public galleries
description: Watch Commons or Lords debates from the public galleries when sitting. Free, with security checks and queues.
tip: Join the queue at St Stephen's Entrance; you may need ID.
checkNote: Only open when Parliament is sitting; check the sitting calendar. Tours cost.

name: Royal Courts of Justice
description: Victorian Gothic courthouse where major civil cases are heard. Public galleries are free; security checks apply.
tip: Check the daily list of cases at the entrance hall.
checkNote: Open weekdays only. Security checks and rules apply.

name: Old Bailey public gallery
description: Watch trials from the public gallery at the Central Criminal Court. Free. Strict rules: no phones, bags or cameras allowed inside.
tip: Leave bags and phones at home; there is no cloakroom.
checkNote: Check before you go: strict rules on phones and bags, age limits and open days apply.

name: UK Supreme Court
description: Visit the UK's highest court, watch hearings and see the building and exhibition. Free to enter with security checks.
tip: Check the site for visiting rules before you travel.
checkNote: Open weekdays only and may be closed on some days; check.

name: Changing the Guard
description: Ceremonial handover of the King's Guard outside Buckingham Palace, with a marching band. Free to watch from the pavements.
tip: Arrive 45 minutes early for a front-row spot.
checkNote: Schedule varies and can be cancelled in bad weather; check the official times.

name: Westminster Cathedral
description: Byzantine-style Catholic cathedral with striped brickwork and mosaics. Free to enter; the tower lift costs.
tip: Go inside the vast nave and look up at the mosaics.
checkNote: Closed during some services; check hours.

name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
description: One of Europe's first traditional Hindu stone temples, carved from marble and limestone. Visitors are welcome free of charge.
tip: Dress modestly and remove shoes in the temple.
checkNote: Opening times and visitor rules vary; check before you go.

name: Southwark Cathedral
description: Gothic cathedral beside Borough Market, with 1,000 years of history and Shakespeare links. Free to enter.
tip: A calm stop between Borough Market and the Thames.
checkNote: Closed for some services and events; check hours.

name: Mudchute Park and Farm
description: A 32-acre city farm and park on the Isle of Dogs, with sheep, goats, llamas and Canary Wharf views. Free to enter.
tip: Bring a picnic; donations to the charity are welcome.
checkNote: Opening days and hours vary; some activities cost.

name: Hackney City Farm
description: A small city farm with pigs, goats, chickens and a cafe in a Victorian yard. Free to enter.
tip: Donations welcome; check the site for family workshops.
checkNote: Closed on some days; check hours.

name: Vauxhall City Farm
description: One of London's oldest city farms, with goats, sheep, pigs and rabbits. Free to enter.
tip: Donations welcome; check the site for family sessions.
checkNote: Opening days vary; check before you go.

name: Spitalfields City Farm
description: Community city farm near Brick Lane with goats, pigs and a community garden. Free to enter.
tip: A quick animal visit before exploring Brick Lane.
checkNote: Hours vary; closed on some days; check before you go.

name: Kentish Town City Farm
description: A hands-on city farm with sheep, goats, pigs and a riding school. Free to enter.
tip: Donations welcome; check for closure days.
checkNote: Closed on some days; check hours.

name: Surrey Docks Farm
description: A riverside city farm with goats, sheep and a smithy in Rotherhithe. Free to enter.
tip: Donations welcome; check the site for opening days.
checkNote: Limited opening days; check before you go.

name: Leake Street Arches
description: A long tunnel under Waterloo station where street artists are allowed to paint. The art changes constantly.
tip: Bring a camera; the art changes every few days.
checkNote: The tunnel can close for events; some events are ticketed.

name: Brick Lane and Shoreditch street art
description: Murals and street art on Brick Lane and the lanes around Shoreditch. A free open-air gallery that changes often.
tip: Look down the side streets for the best pieces.
checkNote: Art changes often; some shops close on Mondays.

name: Greenwich Foot Tunnel
description: A 1902 tiled foot tunnel under the Thames from Greenwich to the Isle of Dogs, with a view of Greenwich from Island Gardens. Free.
tip: Walk through, then look back at Greenwich from Island Gardens.
checkNote: Lifts at both ends; check they are working. Stairs can be steep.

name: Woolwich Ferry
description: A free vehicle and foot ferry across the Thames between Woolwich and North Woolwich, with river views. Free to ride.
tip: Take your bike or buggy; it is a short free river trip.
checkNote: Service times vary and the ferry can be suspended; check TfL.

name: parkrun (free weekly 5k)
description: A free weekly 5k run or walk in many London parks on Saturday mornings. Register once on the website.
tip: Walkers are welcome; most events start at about 9am.
checkNote: Pick an event near you on the website. Start times vary.
